Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue report states that StringUtils methods do not handle Unicode 2.0+ supplementary characters correctly. Specifically, the test case uses strings representing Unicode supplementary characters (U+20000 and U+20001) encoded as surrogate pairs in UTF-16 ("\uD840\uDC00" and "\uD840\uDC01"). The failing test is for the method StringUtils.containsAny(CharSequence, char[]).

Looking at the implementation of containsAny(CharSequence, char[]), the method iterates over the input CharSequence character by character, extracting each char individually via charAt(i). Then it compares this char to each char in the searchChars array. This approach does not correctly handle supplementary Unicode characters because they are represented as surrogate pairs using two char values in UTF-16 — one high surrogate and one low surrogate. Checking character-by-character will lead to matching individual halves of supplementary characters rather than the entire code point.

Since containsAny simply compares individual char values, it will fail to properly identify supplementary characters as whole entities and will mistakenly report matches or misses, as in the failing test.

Thus, the root cause of the failure is that the containsAny method compares char units instead of full Unicode code points when dealing with supplementary characters encoded as surrogate pairs. This leads to incorrect matching behavior for Unicode 2.0+ supplementary characters.

Next, it would be useful to check for other containsAny overloads or utility methods handling this logic, or any code comments related to supplementary character handling.

The code iterates over chars in the CharSequence and compares against chars in the searchChar array. Since Java char is UTF-16 code unit, this method fails to treat surrogate pairs together as a single supplementary character. This causes invalid matching for supplementary Unicode code points.

Hence, diagnosis is that the containsAny(CharSequence, char[]) method has incorrect logic which works only on UTF-16 code units and not full Unicode code points. This results in incorrect handling of any Unicode characters beyond U+FFFF that require surrogate pairs.

No other containsAny method currently handles full supplementary character matching. The root cause is the algorithm comparing char vs char for containsAny, which must be substituted by comparison using code points or handling surrogate pairs correctly.

The evidence from the failing test, bug report, and code review strongly indicates the bug is in containsAny(CharSequence, char[]).
